match.reason: The closest bank point, bus-performance-management, covers performance management in general (goal setting, review, feedback) but does not teach the specific methods the new point names (management by objectives, appraisals, self-evaluation and observation), so it is broader than the new point and would need more than small changes.

draft.title: Performance management
card: Performance management is how a business sets goals for staff, then measures how well each person meets them. It aims to lift the work of individuals and so of the whole business.
a manager and employee agree on clear, measurable goals, such as a sales target, then check progress against them.
a formal review, often once or twice a year, where a manager rates an employee's work against set standards and gives feedback.
the employee rates their own work against the goals. Observation is when a manager watches the employee at work and notes how they perform.
draft.remember: Performance management sets goals, then measures staff against them using several methods.

a.q: Which of these is the best example of management by objectives?
opts: Ravi and his manager agree on a target, then check progress
Ravi's manager watches him serve customers for an hour
Ravi completes a form rating his own work this year
Ravi's manager gives him a yearly rating on a set form
a.why: Management by objectives means agreeing on measurable goals and then checking progress against them. Watching Ravi at work is observation, and the yearly rating on a form is an appraisal, which reviews work against standards but does not start by agreeing goals.
a.clue: Look for the option where the goal is agreed first.

b.q: Mia runs a bakery in Ballarat. Each year she sits with each baker, rates their work against set standards and gives feedback. Which method is this?
b.why: A formal review where a manager rates work against standards and gives feedback is an appraisal. Management by objectives is the most tempting wrong answer, but it centres on goals agreed beforehand and checked over time, not on a review meeting.
b.clue: Who does the rating, and is it a formal review?

a.best: Ravi and his manager agree on a target, then check progress
